name: Mamasa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_quote: In this section we will first examine word stress and then intonation. 4.1 Stress. Stress in Mamasa is not phonemic. Normally the penultimate syllable of a word is stressed (except in the case of the rather rare one-syllable word). ... There is one exception to this stress rule. Vocatives are always stressed on the final syllable of the word.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passages are verbatim in the Matti 1991 PDF we hold at printed pp. 66-67 (pp. 14-15), exactly as the record's the domain quotation/the domain locator/sources state. (2) The classification fixed-strict penultimate (penultimate stress) at word domain is exactly what Matti describes: non-phonemic penultimate stress, recomputed over suffixes, not over enclitics, with final stress only in vocatives (a morphologically conditioned exception, not a lexical contrast) and /ai/ behaving as a diphthong before possessive suffixes (bái-ku), which Matti handles by ordering diphthongisation before stress (p.60-61, section 6). None of this disturbs the classification. (3) Deciding source is a dedicated 1991 SIL phonology article by the language's principal describer; Glottolog lists no grammar, dissertation, or later phonology for Mamasa, so it is the best available and it is.
